## Sources and scope

The chapter uses the repository's saved UNHCR application and decision CSVs for 2000–2025. Three figures are extracted from the verified notebook; the coverage chart is calculated from the same CSV snapshots.

The pending-stock figure comes from the notebook's saved UNHCR population-API output. Its retrieval time is recorded below. It should not be assumed to have the same revision date as the historical CSVs.

{{< include _provenance.qmd >}}

## Persons, cases, and events

The application and decision series include only rows whose reporting unit is **P (persons)**. Rows marked **C (cases)** are excluded; no case-size multiplier is applied. A country can change units between years, changing which records enter the subset.

Application events are not a count of unique individuals across the study period. The source distinguishes new applications, repeats, appeals, and other types. Missing type codes are retained as Other / unspecified.

The pending-stock series is a separate population measure. It is not restricted to precisely the same country-year reports as the flow charts.

## Decision shares and recognition rates {#decision-rates}

Let **R** be recognised refugee-status decisions, **C** complementary-protection decisions, **J** rejections, and **A** administrative closures.

| Measure | Numerator | Denominator |
|---|---|---|
| Recognised share of all decisions, used in the chart | R | All recorded decisions, including A |
| Refugee recognition rate among substantive decisions | R | R + C + J |
| Total protection rate among substantive decisions | R + C | R + C + J |

The chart uses annual decision counts. It does not follow an application cohort. Composition can change with the mix of reporting countries, applicants, and procedures.

Definitions follow the [UNHCR asylum statistics explainer](https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/insights/explainers/forcibly-displaced-faq.html). Administrative closures are not necessarily substantive refusals.

## Reporting coverage

The coverage chart counts distinct receiving-country ISO codes with at least one persons-reported row in each file and year. It counts presence, not completeness. It does not verify that every reporter submitted all procedures or a complete annual return.

Codes are not necessarily a fixed set over time. Records can describe historical or special entities; the chart therefore uses “receiving-country codes.”

## Checks used in the analysis

- Validate reporting units and check for negative volumes.
- Preserve raw totals through grouping.
- Retain rows with unspecified application type.
- Aggregate application types before joining to avoid duplicated decisions.
- Retain decision-only rows through an outer join.
- Check that both totals are independently conserved.
- Refuse preparation when code or input snapshots differ from the verified execution.

## Reproduce the sample

Run these commands from the python-charts repository:

    python scripts/prepare_quarto_preview.py
    quarto preview quarto-preview

Preparation reads the executed notebook and local CSVs, checks their identities, extracts three figures, and generates the coverage figure and supporting text. It does not download fresh data or rerun the notebook.

For a new analytical edition, first refresh and verify the notebook using its execution script. Review changes in coverage and source revisions before refreshing this publication.

## Limitations and reuse

This is descriptive analysis without causal inference or uncertainty estimates. Missing reports, procedural differences, revisions, and changes in reporting units affect interpretation. Missing or zero pending-stock totals are treated as unavailable for the notebook plot; that plotting choice does not establish the meaning of every source zero.

Consult [UNHCR's methodology](https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/methodology) and [dataset terms](https://www.unhcr.org/what-we-do/data-and-publications/data-and-statistics/terms-use-datasets) before reusing figures. Cite the original sources alongside this independent analysis.

## Explorer updates

The [country explorer](explore.qmd) uses separate dated snapshots refreshed from
UNHCR weekly and on publication updates. The narrative chapter above stays pinned
to its verified notebook edition. Each refresh requests years from 2000 through
the previous calendar year, validates grouping keys, counts, and units, and checks
that aggregation preserves totals. A coverage loss greater than 20% against the
committed baseline stops publication for review.

The two datasets are aggregated independently by receiving country, year, and
unit, then combined with an outer join. Missing observations remain unavailable.
Percentages appear only where all four outcomes reconcile to a positive total.
No smoothing or case-to-person conversion is applied in the explorer.

Download time records retrieval, not the source release date. A latest available
year may be incomplete. UNHCR links retrieve current country data, which can differ
from the stored snapshot. The chart CSV and source ZIP identify the displayed data.
